title: Multi-Convergence-Angle Ptychography for Biological Imaging with Simultaneous Strong Contrast and High Resolution
content: Structural biology, pivotal for deciphering the tertiary structures of biological molecules, has propelled significant advancements in disease research, drug development, and the exploration of fundamental biological processes. The growing need for accurate three-dimensional structural analysis through single-particle analysis (SPA) or electron tomography (ET) underscores the importance of obtaining high-quality two-dimensional projection images that exhibit both strong contrast and high resolution. Nonetheless, imaging unstained biological specimens poses considerable challenges, primarily due to their light elemental composition and heightened sensitivity to electron radiation, which limits the electron dose and leads to diminished contrast. Although phase contrast imaging at high defocus [1, 2] or phase plates [3, 4] are frequently employed to enhance contrast, these techniques often sacrifice high-resolution information or dampen high-frequency signals, creating a significant void in the quest for achieving both strong contrast and high resolution simultaneously.
